note.note:
History:
• Chief concerns: Persistent low mood, low energy, poor appetite (~3.5 months), episodic palpitations/subjective shortness of breath mainly in elevators, and unintended weight loss (~1 stone over ~6 months).  
• Associated symptoms: Intermittent nausea; no vomiting, no diarrhoea, no blood or mucus per rectum, no chest pain, no acid reflux.  
• Functional impact: Decreased participation in “nightly activities,” reduced physical activity at home and work; occasionally headaches and nausea at work.  
• Triggers: Palpitations/SOB most noticeable in lifts; not clearly exertional when walking (patient later noted limited recent walking).  
• Timeline: Appetite ↓ and low mood began after starting new law-firm position (~3–3.5 mo ago). Weight loss preceded appetite change (≈6 mo).  
• Previous episodes: None reported.

Past Medical History:
• Hypothyroidism (under-active thyroid).  
• Medications: Levothyroxine (thyroxine) – previously taken; currently stopped (dose/route/frequency not documented). No other regular medicines disclosed.  
• Allergies: Not documented.  
• Recent labs/monitoring: None since switching physicians.

Physical Examination:
(Tele-visit – no in-person exam performed)  
• Patient alert, conversational.  
• Reports no chest pain, no vomiting, no diarrhoea, no rectal bleeding, no mucous, no overt respiratory distress.  
• No objective vitals available.

Impression:
Low mood, fatigue, weight loss, palpitations – likely multifactorial; differentials include uncontrolled thyroid dysfunction (off levothyroxine), anaemia, metabolic or nutritional deficiency; depression also suspected.

Management Plan:
• Order comprehensive blood work: CBC, renal and liver profile, thyroid panel, iron studies, B-12/folate, vitamin D, ± glucose as per standard “general set of bloods.”  
• Patient instructed to phone support number in app to schedule phlebotomy; physician to complete requisition.  
• Results to be returned via text prompt; patient to book follow-up review of results.  
• Safety-netting: Attend Emergency Department for any acute chest pain, severe palpitations, or sudden shortness of breath. Re-contact service for new vomiting or change in bowel habit.  
• Consider full physical examination and further work-up (e.g., ECG, imaging) after blood results.

Patient Summary:
35-year-old man with history of hypothyroidism (off medication) presents with 3–6 months of low mood, poor appetite, weight loss, and lift-related palpitations/SOB. Initial plan is screening blood tests to assess thyroid status, anaemia, and general metabolic causes before in-person evaluation.

Key Takeaways:
1. Arrange blood test promptly by calling the 0300 support number in the app.  
2. Restarting or adjusting thyroid medication will be considered once blood results are available; no self-adjustment for now.  
3. Seek urgent care for chest pain, severe palpitations, or new gastrointestinal bleeding/vomiting.

Next Steps:
• Complete blood work within the next week.  
• Schedule virtual or in-person follow-up once results available.  
• Possible referral for ECG and physical examination depending on findings.
